Have you test driven this for actual dev work for longer time on a real project?

This needs very careful testing whether running two editor instances on the same project leads to errors regarding interaction with the `.godot` folder. Are we aware of any such standing issues?

Also this might break some updating functionality in the editor instance which is not used for the LSP, since the LSP force reloads some scripts when the external editor saves them.

Funny! I started implement it on my side! I have a problem with your implementation because the godot executable output on stdout. Shouldn't it be reserved for lsp stdio communication ?

Just to check that I got this properly.
> This command line argument should definitely overwrite the network/language_server/use_thread and network/language_server/show_native_symbols_in_editor editor settings. Both of them make no sense for a headless instance.

When you say overwrite, I guess you are saying that both settings values must be ignored and use `false` as their value when LSP stdio mode is on.

> When adding this we should implement the shutdown and exit endpoints to support protocol compliant shutdown.

This PR should also add support for [shutdown](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#shutdown) and [exit](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#exit) on the LSP server, right?

> As far as I can see this does not redirect print somewhere else? I wonder whether this might be a problem for some clients.

No, the code is not doing any kind of redirection of print. As far I can tell that is not a problem for Helix editor, and I assume that other LSP clients ignore output outside the one that follows LSP protocol. Maybe we can get help from other members of the community that use editors that support LSP over stdio. If I recall correctly Godot can log to a file when runs a game, so maybe we can leverage that. Let me know what do you think about this, I don't want to make this PR more complex if most LSP clients are good citizens (I'm optimistic about LSP implementations 😉)

> Is stderr logged to some place? If users run into issues with this headless instance we need clear infos to debug this. LSP traces only capture network communication, not errors deeper in the Server implementation (we do not forward all errors to the client).

The code in this PR is not changing or doing anything with stderr, so what is currently being sent to stderr should continue being sent to stderr.

> > This command line argument should definitely overwrite the network/language_server/use_thread and network/language_server/show_native_symbols_in_editor editor settings. Both of them make no sense for a headless instance.
> 
> When you say overwrite, I guess you are saying that both settings values must be ignored and use `false` as their value when LSP stdio mode is on.

Yes, if the editor is headless it should be no problem to block the main thread and displaying documentation would be pointless.

> > When adding this we should implement the shutdown and exit endpoints to support protocol compliant shutdown.
> 
> This PR should also add support for [shutdown](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#shutdown) and [exit](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#exit) on the LSP server, right?

Yeah. I'd like to avoid dangling headless processes and I don't really trust that all editors out there will force shutdown the process if we don't implement a graceful shutdown. Idk if there is anything meaningful we can do in `shutdown`, but it should at least be there to prevent error responses. And `exit` must stop the process.

> > As far as I can see this does not redirect print somewhere else? I wonder whether this might be a problem for some clients.
> 
> No, the code is not doing any kind of redirection of print. As far I can tell that is not a problem for Helix editor, and I assume that other LSP clients ignore output outside the one that follows LSP protocol. Maybe we can get help from other members of the community that use editors that support LSP over stdio. If I recall correctly Godot can log to a file when runs a game, so maybe we can leverage that. Let me know what do you think about this, I don't want to make this PR more complex if most LSP clients are good citizens (I'm optimistic about LSP implementations 😉)

I'm not :sweat_smile: I'd like ensure that at least Zed (that one seems to work), Emacs and some Neovim setup handles that correctly. VSCode and Rider use plugins to manage the connection, so I don't think we need to check those in particular.

> > Is stderr logged to some place? If users run into issues with this headless instance we need clear infos to debug this. LSP traces only capture network communication, not errors deeper in the Server implementation (we do not forward all errors to the client).
> 
> The code in this PR is not changing or doing anything with stderr, so what is currently being sent to stderr should continue being sent to stderr.

That's not the issue. The issue is how users can conveniently access stderr when reporting issues. In the end it depends on what the editor does with it at the moment. So I want to at least confirm that the popular editors log it somewhere.

> That's not the issue. The issue is how users can conveniently access stderr when reporting issues. In the end it depends on what the editor does with it at the moment. So I want to at least confirm that the popular editors log it somewhere.

In the case of `helix`, you can see the logs with [:log-open](https://docs.helix-editor.com/commands.html?highlight=logs#typable-commands)
Here is an example
```
2025-11-03T16:23:11.329 helix_lsp::transport [ERROR] godot err <- "handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11\n"
2025-11-03T16:23:11.329 helix_lsp::transport [ERROR] godot err <- "Engine version: Godot Engine v4.6.dev.custom_build (0fdbf050e0c7fc7e0a9d42c2a41ee3bfdffbd8f1)\n"
2025-11-03T16:23:11.329 helix_lsp::transport [ERROR] godot err <- "Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug on: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues\n"
2025-11-03T16:23:16.972 helix_lsp::transport [ERROR] godot err <- "[1] 1   libsystem_platform.dylib            0x0000000191e396a4 _sigtramp + 56\n"
```

In the case of `neovim` the [docs](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lsp.html#_lua-module:-vim.lsp.log) says that are stored on the LSP log file (see the Note)

In the case of `emacs`, [`eglot` docs](https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/eglot.html#Troubleshooting-Eglot) mentions an `eglot-stderr-buffer`

In the case of `zed`, [the Ruby LSP docs](https://zed.dev/docs/languages/ruby?highlight=lsp%20logs#language-servers) mention `dev: Open Language Server Logs` command. My assumption is that is available for all LSP.

I'm not a user of `neovim`, `emacs` or `zed` so take the previous mentions with care (it's just me Googling docs)

Hope this helps with your concerns.

It currently doesn't work on neovim but I may have misconfigured it. 


I properly enabled it my my `lspconfig.lua` and it successfully connected to the TCP version:

```
vim.lsp.enable("gdscript")
```

Unfortunately I failed to override the `cmd` parameter in `lsp/gdscript.lua`:

```lua
return {
	cmd = {
		"/path/to/godot.macos.editor.dev.arm64",
		"--lsp",
		"--headless",
		"--log-file",
		"/path/to/debug.log",
		"/path/to/my/project.godot",
	},
}
```

I disabled it and run it "manually" by adding the following file `plugin/mylsp.lua` : 

```lua
local project_godot_path = vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/project.godot"
if vim.fn.filereadable(project_godot_path) then
	vim.lsp.start({
		name = "educational lsp",
		cmd = {
          		"/path/to/godot.macos.editor.dev.arm64",
        		"--lsp",
	        	"--headless",
        		"--log-file",
	    	        "/path/to/debug.log",
			project_godot_path,
		},
		on_attach = function(client, _) vim.notify("GDScript LSP: Connected successfully", vim.log.levels.INFO) end,
		on_error = function(err) vim.notify("GDScript LSP: Failed to start client: " .. err, vim.log.levels.ERROR) end,
	})
end
```

Unfortunately, the only method exchanged are "initialize" and "initialized" (after logging in `JSONRPC::process_action()`.
Just for information I manage to override the `nvim-lspconfig` by moving my custom `lsp/gdscript.lua` configuration to `after/lsp/gdscript.lua`.

The new logger related changes don't seem correct to me.

Shouldn't we just have a dedicated `LspLogger` for this situation that does this job, instead of shoehorning an stdout via stderr feature into the generalized logger interface?

Keep in mind that in the future we might want to route logging through https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#window_logMessage

As far I can tell, we can add an `LSPLogger` and set it as the logger on `main.cpp` if `--lsp` flag is present without issues.
Also, if the plan is to route logs to LSP clients in the future, we can keep `LSPLogger` simple and don't deal with colored output for now (this will let us avoid handling OS specifics around colored output)

We have code review and build systems using llm and lsp server allows it to inspect failed ci and investigate to give intelligent error message summary and better code review. Jenkins driven. Ability for Jenkins job to fire up lsp on demand is super handy

I think this is a good feature for the case of 

- isolated run on CI
- ExternalEditor + visible GodotEditor with LSP stdio

Would not work for the case of ExternalEditor + headless Godot LSP + visible GodotEditor.

1. Two instances competing for the .godot/ cache and project.godot file can cause dialog about external changes.
2. Unless manually remapped, the headless instance will occupy the default DAP port.
3. Running a secondary full engine process (even headless) just for text-parsing is inefficient.

Probably such case is out of scope of this PR, so I am just sharing my concern.
Please also see the proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/13490#discussioncomment-16719432
